timeline.result: Started investigating payments-api.
p99 latency 8.4s and 5xx at 11.2%. CPU ~35%, JVM heap normal. Nothing obvious.
Errors dropped for ~3 minutes, then came straight back.

timeline.action: Escalated to Priya Sharma (Staff Engineer, Payments)
timeline.result: Priya joined the incident call.

timeline.action: Grepped application logs for database errors
timeline.result: Found HikariPool 'Connection is not available' timeouts. Pool at 50/50 active with 212 threads waiting.
timeline.command: kubectl -n payments logs deploy/payments-api --since=15m | grep HikariPool

timeline.result: recon-job was holding 38 long-running connections since 02:00; Midnight Deals retries were using the rest.
timeline.command: SELECT application_name, state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY 1,2;

timeline.result: Waiting threads dropped to 0 within 2 minutes; 5xx falling.
timeline.command: helm upgrade payments-api charts/payments-api -n payments --reuse-values --set db.hikari.maximumPoolSize=100

timeline.result: p99 back to ~380ms, 5xx below 0.1%.
Customer impact ended; monitoring normal.

failed_attempts.result: Errors dropped for ~3 minutes, then came straight back.

root_cause: The nightly recon-job (02:00 IST) held ~38 long-running Postgres connections while Midnight Deals payment retries needed the rest. The HikariCP pool of 50 was exhausted, so requests waited 30s and failed with 503.
resolution: Priya raised the HikariCP pool from 50 to 100. Latency recovered within minutes.
action_items: Move recon-job out of the 02:00 window (PAY-1043, not started)
Alert on HikariCP waiting threads > 20 (PAY-1044)
customer_impact: ~9% of payment attempts failed for 52 minutes (~2,300 failed checkouts).
postmortem_summary: payments-api latency spike and failed payments during Midnight Deals - payments-api, SEV1, 09 Jun 2026, 02:41 IST. Impact: ~9% of payment attempts failed for 52 minutes (~2,300 failed checkouts). Root cause: The nightly recon-job (02:00 IST) held ~38 long-running Postgres connections while Midnight Deals payment retries needed the rest. The HikariCP pool of 50 was exhausted, so requests waited 30s and failed with 503. What did NOT work: Restarted payments-api pods (Errors dropped for ~3 minutes, then came straight back.). What fixed it: Priya raised the HikariCP pool from 50 to 100. Latency recovered within minutes. Resolved by Priya Sharma in 52 minutes. Follow-ups: Move recon-job out of the 02:00 window (PAY-1043, not started); Alert on HikariCP waiting threads > 20 (PAY-1044).

timeline.result: Started investigating orders-service.

timeline.command: psql -h postgres-main-replica-1 -c "SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() AS lag;"
